thread:
incident-bot: Pager alert triggered: possible PII exposure from customer-metadata-service -> /users/meta (severity: P2). Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/8962 :rotating_light:
ash: oncall here, looking now. seeing elevated 5xx + a sensitive-log spike.
dave: paging db team + security. can you confirm which tables exported?
maria: I pulled the logs. looks like a bad join in the nightly export job touched `user_backup` and `analytics_events` between 2026-03-14T02:12:00Z and 2026-03-14T02:18:30Z. possible rows with email/phone hashed but `address` was plain text. attaching sample sanitized row below.
```
{"user_id":"REDACTED","email":"redacted@example.com","phone":"REDACTED","address":"123 MAIN ST"}
```
sanjay: oof. so limited to the backup export job only, not API reads?
maria: confirmed — no API paths implicated in tracing. export pipeline (kafka -> batch-export job) is the vector.
ash: mitigation plan: 1) stop export job 2) revoke temp credentials 3) rotate export S3 bucket keys 4) snapshot scope for comms. doing 1 now.
incident-bot: export job stop succeeded (run id: batch-20260314-42).
dave: tagging as potential security/privacy incident. @security-liaison please confirm severity class and customer impact template.
security-liaison: initial assessment: estimated ~1.3k rows, approx 450 unique customer accounts. data fields possibly exposed: address (plain), order_id, partial product history. no SSN/CC detected in quick scan. marking as PII but not high-risk (no financial IDs). recommend notifying affected customers and posting status page.
legal-jane: quick note — we'll need to include timing, scope, and mitigation steps. avoid words like "breach" until we confirm third-party access. run of show: draft customer notice -> legal approval -> send via support + email for affected users.
ops-oncall: keys revoked and bucket access revoked. I also created a read-only snapshot of the bucket for investigation: s3://redwood-investigation-snapshots/batch-20260314-42
ash: for comms, here's a short status page draft. feedback pls.
```
Status: Investigating (Mar 14 02:12 UTC)
Impact: An internal batch export job may have written customer address fields to a backup location.
What we're doing: Job stopped, keys rotated, security & legal investigating scope.
Next update: in 60 minutes.
```
maria: suggest adding "no evidence of external access" if we confirm. else keep neutral.
dave: agree. keep conservative: "no evidence of external access to date" — ok to include if we finish quick audit.
ash: customer notification draft (for affected accounts) — please review: 
```
Subject: Important: Notice regarding a limited data exposure affecting some account backups
Hello,
We are writing to let you know about an incident we discovered on Mar 14, 2026 involving an internal batch export that may have written limited account backup data (including address) to an internal backup bucket.
What happened: An export job wrote a subset of customer backup rows to a snapshot. The job has been stopped and access keys have been revoked.
What data may have been included: address, order_id, product metadata. We have not found evidence of social security numbers, credit card numbers, or other high-risk financial identifiers.
What we are doing: rotating keys, auditing access logs, and will notify you if we discover any external access. We will also provide remediation steps and an FAQ in the next communication.
Next steps: We will send another update within 24 hours and provide contact info for support and a dedicated incident channel.
Regards,
Redwood Inference Security Team
```
security-liaison: wording looks reasonable. add: "We are offering complimentary identity monitoring for affected accounts for 90 days" only if legal approves.
legal-jane: pls remove any offer language until procurement OKs budget. instead say "we are evaluating protective options and will provide details if applicable."
maria: internal note for timeline: only data between 02:12 and 02:18:30 UTC. starting offset: batch-key=b-20260314-42.
dave: quick ask: can we enumerate third-party access to the snapshot? were any external IAM principals granted? ops-oncall: no external principals, only internal service accounts existed; CloudTrail shows no GetObject from outside our VPC. I will attach the CT logs to the investigation ticket.
ash: next actions: 1) security run full scan for any sensitive fields (in progress) 2) legal to review customer notice and approve 3) prepare status page and support template 4) prepare affected-account list (by 03:30 UTC).
incident-bot: on-call handoff scheduled: @ash -> @dave at 03:00 UTC.
ash: support template for CS to use (short):
```
Hi <Customer>,
We are investigating an internal export that may have included limited account data. We are actively investigating and will share a timeline and remediation steps. If you have urgent concerns, reply to this message or contact support@redwood.ai.
```
ops-oncall: adding automation to block future batch exports until config validation is added (I filed infra-issue #1147).
sanjay: pls confirm whether we need to escalate to regulators. legal-jane: we need scope + verification of external access before deciding on regulator notification. log that question and aim to decide within 24 hours.
ash: can security confirm expected exposure count for the notice? security-liaison: preliminary: ~450 accounts, accuracy +-10%. will confirm.
ash: manual approval: @legal-jane can you sign off on sending customer notice once you receive final numbers?
legal-jane: yes I'll review ASAP upon final scope.
maria: final scan attached to ticket shows no external access and 468 affected accounts.
security-liaison: confirming: 468 accounts affected, exposures limited to address/order_id/product metadata, no high-risk identifiers found. recommend sending notice with "no evidence of external access to date."
legal-jane: approved language with that sentence included, and timeframe updated. ok to send to affected customers.
\.dave: ok go ahead. @ops-oncall can you create the support thread and queue messages for tomorrow's business day as well?
ops-oncall: support thread created and notification scheduled. status page updated to "Investigating -> Identified" with final text and link to FAQ draft.
ash: thank you everyone. log: incident severity set to P2-security, tracking ticket INC-20260314-74.
incident-bot: Incident closed for paging; follow-ups: postmortem due in 7 days, and communication archive created at https://confluence.redwood/internal/incidents/INC-20260314-74 :white_check_mark:
